Playbook.name: Windows — Potential Port Monitor or Print Processor Registration Abuse - SOC Playbook

ExecutiveSummary.Overview: A print Port Monitor or Print Processor registry entry was created/changed - registering a DLL that the spooler (SYSTEM) loads, a persistence + privilege-escalation technique. Triage question: attacker spooler persistence, or a legitimate printer-driver install?
ExecutiveSummary.BusinessImpact: A malicious port monitor/print processor DLL runs as SYSTEM via the spooler on every boot - persistent SYSTEM execution.

TelemetryRequirements.Requirement: Windows Security + Sysmon + PowerShell logs via Elastic Agent (verified live). Sysmon event.code 1=process(command_line/parent populated), 11=file, 13/12=registry(registry.path populated); process.code_signature NOT collected.

Signal.Name: Port monitor/print processor abuse
Signal.Details: Sysmon registry write (event 13/12) to the Print Monitors/Environments key.

Input.name: $hostname
Input.description: Host where the registry key changed.

InitialAssessment.Rule: Weigh the evidence story, not any single fact - see ClassificationGuidance.

Investigation.Goal: Determine whether the registry modification is malicious port monitor/print processor abuse or a legitimate change.

Step.name: Confirm the registry write, value, data and writing process
Step.Purpose: The writing process, value and data distinguish attacker persistence from legitimate config.
Step.Query: FROM logs-windows.sysmon_operational-* | WHERE event.code IN ("13","12") AND host.name == "$hostname" AND @timestamp >= NOW() - 4 hours | WHERE registry.path RLIKE "(?i).*.*control.*print.*(monitors|environments).*" | KEEP @timestamp, process.name, registry.path, registry.value, registry.data.strings, user.name | SORT @timestamp DESC | LIMIT 20
Step.AnalystNotes: A DLL registered as a port monitor/print processor from a non-standard path by a non-installer process is persistence.

Step.name: Process context on the host
Step.Purpose: The writing process's parent/origin reveals whether this was attacker-driven or a legitimate installer.
Step.Query: FROM logs-windows.sysmon_operational-*,logs-system.security-* | WHERE event.code IN ("1","4688") AND host.name == "$hostname" AND @timestamp >= NOW() - 2 hours | STATS runs = COUNT(*), parents = VALUES(process.parent.name), users = VALUES(user.name) BY process.name | SORT runs DESC | LIMIT 15
Step.AnalystNotes: A registry write by a script/LOLBin/unknown process is attacker persistence; a write by a signed installer/OS process is likely benign.

Node.Condition: A port-monitor/print-processor DLL registered from a temp/user path or by a suspicious process.
A signed installer/OS process making the change under a known context.
A print-management tool re-registering components after an update.
Registry change with unclear writing process/intent.

DocumentationChecklist.Item: Attach outputs of INV-01-REG-WRITE, INV-02-REG-CONTEXT to the case.

SOCAction.Item: Confirm the software/change; close as false_positive.

Indicators.Item: A port-monitor/print-processor DLL registered from a temp/user path or by a suspicious process..

SOCAction.Item: Remove the malicious registry entry; isolate the host; open IR.
Hunt the same key change estate-wide.

Misconfiguration.Definition: A legitimate printer-driver installation registering its components.

Indicators.Item: A print-management tool re-registering components after an update.

Phase.name: Immediate Actions (0-30 minutes)
Phase.Action: Confirm the activity on the host; if malicious indicators, isolate the host.
Identify the responsible account/process and its origin.

Phase.name: Containment and Eradication (hours)
Phase.Action: Isolate the host; capture volatile evidence; hunt the same pattern across the estate.
Reset credentials used on the host if compromise is confirmed.

Phase.name: Recovery and Hardening (days)
Phase.Action: Remediate the root cause; add/verify EDR coverage; apply relevant hardening.

QualityChecks.Check: Confirm the required telemetry (Sysmon/Security auditing) is present on the host.
Tune known-benign administrative sources via exceptions, not by disabling the rule.

TruePositiveClosure.Item: Host contained and triaged; root cause eradicated; estate swept; findings recorded.
